name: Putinism
summary: Putinism is the loose governing outlook of Vladimir Putin's Russia, which scholars describe as a strong centralised state, great-power status, sovereignty against the West and conservative Orthodox values. Putin's own interviews and the CSIS report give positions on democracy abroad, privatization, nuclear deterrence, family, patriotic education and the Church, but little on most economic or constitutional questions.
scope: Putinism as the scholars who name it (Migranyan, Glinski, Aron, Snegovaya and colleagues) describe it, and Putin's own words in his interviews with Oliver Stone and his 2021 essay. Putin denies Russia has a state ideology, so only positions stated by him or described by those scholars are answered; policy inferred from Wikipedia summaries is not.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Putin accuses the United States of backing separatists and terrorists in the Northern Caucasus and asks why partners receive them officially.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Putin defines democracy as a policy based on the will of the people, known through voting, though he applies it mostly to Crimea.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Putin defends the Crimea referendum as the way to know the people's will, saying the choice of the people has to be respected.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Putin says Russia is not building military blocs with China and calls NATO a remnant of the Cold War.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Putin stresses that Russia is a multi-ethnic, multi-religious country built over centuries.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Putin says Russia has started extracting hydrocarbons in the Arctic seas and that disputes should be settled under international law.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Putin says Russia and China run joint projects in peaceful nuclear energy.

force-without-un.rationale: Putin says force abroad is sometimes necessary but better done at a government's invitation or under international law with a UN Security Council decision.

foreign-policy-non-interference.rationale: Putin objects to the US imposing democracy by force and to American diplomats funding Russian opposition rallies, which he treats as interference in internal affairs.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The CSIS report records explicitly homophobic and transphobic rhetoric at the centre of Putin's statements since 2022.

gradual-change.rationale: Putin says Russia's new political stage began only in the 1990s and should develop gradually from its thousand-year state tradition.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Putin's essay grounds Russian claims in a shared historical and spiritual heritage with Ukraine and treats historical lands as the basis for present claims.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The CSIS report says Surkov made the correct use of Russian history in education a matter of vital national interest.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Putin says Russia has and keeps its nuclear capabilities and treats the nuclear balance as essential, including against missile defence near its borders.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Putin says nuclear balance matters and that trying to destroy it is a great mistake; Russia has kept its capabilities and a right to leave arms treaties.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The essay says Russians, Ukrainians and Belarusians are one people with common roots and faith, whose division was imposed.

more-religion-public.rationale: The CSIS report says the Russian Orthodox Church became increasingly present at state ceremonies and in state structures.

national-self-determination.rationale: Putin defends the Crimea vote by saying democracy is the will of the people and that the International Court's Kosovo opinion supports a nation's self-determination.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Putin says he told big business leaders it was to assume more social responsibility.

one-party-rule.rationale: Putin tells Stone that one party's monopoly is pernicious to the country and that the Soviet system's frozen politics was a dead end.

party-controls-media.rationale: The CSIS report describes state propaganda and attacks on independent news outlets as core Kremlin practice.

patriotic-education.rationale: The CSIS report describes a State Program for Patriotic Education whose budget has grown, with patriotic clubs in schools.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The CSIS report says the Kremlin's ideology rests on Russia as a civilization state guarding traditional values and cultural heritage.

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: Putin says it is wrong to impose one's own standards on other nations, that democracy cannot be imported, and that imposing it by force is senseless and damaging.

property-fundamental.rationale: Putin says he told the oligarchs the government would protect their property and that the law is the law, while insisting the laws on it be fair.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Putin says that when the Soviet Union broke up, 25 million Russians suddenly found themselves abroad, and treats this as a central grievance.

public-ownership.rationale: Putin says he did not stop privatization, only made it fairer, and that reversing it would damage the economy and ordinary people more than the original sales did.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The CSIS report records the repression of NGOs and human rights activists and the criminal use of 'foreign agent' labels.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Putin's essay says Russia was robbed by the Soviet breakup and treats the borders as arbitrary.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Putin's essay argues that Russians and Ukrainians are one people divided by borders imposed by Bolshevik decisions and outside interests.

rich-first.rationale: Putin says Russian financial and economic policy aims to even out living standards and incomes across all regions and citizens, though not fully.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The CSIS report says the Kremlin's conservative turn rests on Christian values set against the West's emphasis on sexual minorities' rights.

small-step-social-reform.rationale: Putin says Russia's political system should develop gradually, building on its inherited state tradition.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Putin says the government pushes investment out of oil and gas and into high-technology and defence industries by administrative and financial means.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Putin says Russia and China are not trying to build any military blocs, and calls NATO a remnant of the Cold War.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The CSIS report says the Kremlin delegitimizes liberal opposition by presenting it as foreign and Western.

traditional-family.rationale: The CSIS report lists traditional family and gender roles among the tenets Putinism guards, against materialism and individualism.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Putin's 2021 essay presents Russians and Ukrainians as one historical people with a continuous thousand-year identity from Rus.

notes: Themes searched in Putin's interviews with Oliver Stone and the CSIS report: economy, government, society, world, liberty, culture, ecology, means. Putin denies Russia has a state ideology, so many economic and constitutional statements have no recorded position. The 2007 Munich speech and Millennium text were not opened. The Wikipedia article was used only to find sources; the committed answers that rested on Wikipedia summaries were nulled or replaced, except the five that rest on Putin's 2021 essay.
